name: Edasich
description: A star 31 parsecs away, 12 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: radius 12.083 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 57.211 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: effective temperature 4570 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.064)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: distance 31.027 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 31 parsecs away, 12 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 57 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,570 K, so 12.083 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 75458: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Iota Draconis
quotes.card: Iota Draconis, also named Edasich, is a star in the northern circumpolar constellation of Draco.
quotes.introduction: A visually unremarkable star of apparent magnitude 3.3, in 2002 it was discovered to have a planet orbiting it.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 1614731957531452544 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
